name: one-simdgroup-through-ten-shuffle-shapes
rationale:
One 32-lane simdgroup, one invocation per lane, reading itself through ten shuffle shapes at once: simd_shuffle_and_fill_up and _down on uint, float, float3 and half4, plus the plain simd_shuffle_up on float3 and simd_shuffle_down on uint2 and half3. Those ten AIR symbols are 178 corpus sources between them and the largest uncovered block left; every corpus host buries them in a loop or a function-constant-gated region, so a fixture is the only way to reach them.

Every lane's datum is its own index plus one and its fill datum is a hundred plus its index, so the 32 data values and the 32 fill values are disjoint and each is distinct: the lane a result came from, and whether it came from the data or the fill operand, are both readable straight off the answer. The four deltas differ (3, 5, 2, 4, 1, 9) so no two of the fill shapes can be confused with each other, and delta 9 on the float shape puts more than a quarter of the group on the fill side. All the values are small integers held exactly by float and by half -- the largest half is 134 and the largest float is 524 -- and the vector lanes scale by two and four, so the whole comparison is exact without depending on any rounding.

The three plain shuffles have no fill operand, and Metal leaves a lane whose source index leaves the simdgroup undefined. Exactly those lanes -- below 6 for the up shuffle, at or above 25 and 27 for the two down shuffles -- have their slots overwritten with zero after the unconditional store, so the case compares only the lanes Metal defines while still making the call on all 32.

name: constant-buffer-float4-to-mrt3-highest
rationale: The loop-free fragment converts the exact finite float4 color in the 32-byte constant buffer to half4 and structurally inserts that same value into all three return members; selecting attachment two verifies the complete three-target aggregate mapping.

name: alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-0
rationale: A tile kernel whose EXPLICIT imageblock carries `air.alias_implicit_imageblock`, so its cell is not tile-local scratch but the render targets themselves. Compared in colour attachment 0. Every lane written is a function of lanes READ from the cell, so a cell that started as undefined scratch answers differently at every texel, and the comparison is made in the attachment, so a cell that never reached one answers differently again. The AIR is the corpus's widest aliased layout byte for byte -- {half4, half4, half}, 24 bytes -- and 30 of the 14579 corpus sources carry the marker in four layouts of which this is one. Lane 0 comes from colour, lane 1 from aux and lane 2 from depth, so answering any plane from the wrong attachment moves the answer. Initial texels are colour = (x, y, x + 16y, 1), aux = (x + 300, y + 300, 600 + x + 16y, 7) and depth = 100 + x + 16y; all 256 are distinct and every result is an integer below 2048, exact in binary16, so no lane depends on rounding, on fast math, or on association. Derived closed form: (x + 1, y + 302, 103 + x + 16y, 2). Metal reproduced it exactly at all 256 texels.

name: alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-1
rationale: The sibling of alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-0 compared in colour attachment 1, which is the SECOND member of the aliased imageblock struct. A single-output case cannot show that a write to member 1 reached attachment 1 rather than attachment 0, so each attachment gets its own case over the same dispatch. Lane 0 comes from aux, lane 1 from colour and lane 2 from depth, so this plane also fails under any attachment permutation. Derived closed form: (2x + 600, y + 4, 300 + 3x + 48y, 12), every lane an integer below 2048 and therefore exact in binary16. Metal reproduced it exactly at all 256 texels.

name: alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-2
rationale: The sibling of alias-a-tile-cell-onto-render-target-0 compared in colour attachment 2, the THIRD member of the aliased struct. This is the case that settles what the member's name does not: the member is typed `half` and the corpus calls it `depth`, and it is still COLOUR attachment 2 -- an r16_float render target -- because it is declared third. Nothing about the mapping keys on a member name. Its value is the sum of the third lane of all three planes, 700 + 3x + 48y, an integer below 2048 and so exact in binary16 whichever way the two additions are associated. Metal reproduced it exactly at all 256 texels.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twelve-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 12 and receives exact float4 zero from all eleven linked _uber_clear bodies. A fourteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eight-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 8 and receives exact float4 zero from all seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A ten-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: one-simdgroup-through-ten-matrix-8x8-shapes
rationale:
One 32-lane simdgroup driving ten `air.simdgroup_matrix_8x8_*` families: the load and store at both float and half, the diagonal init at both, and the multiply-accumulate at all four precision mixes the corpus uses. Every matrix holds small integers, so every product and sum is exact at half as well as float and no rounding decision is involved.

The first accumulate is the only non-trivial matmul and it is deliberately asymmetric: B is a cyclic column shift, so `A*B + C` rotates A's columns before adding C and neither a transposed load nor a swapped `A*B` / `B*A` reproduces it. Row 0 of the result is 107, 101, 103 ... 113 while column 0 is 107, 123, 139 ... 219. The other four accumulate against a diagonal, which isolates the precision mix from the matmul: `Ah*I + C` and `A*I + C` must answer the SAME 64 words even though one takes its left operand at half and the other at float, so a mix that widens the wrong operand shows up as a disagreement between two slots of one output.

The results are stored to device scratch and read back through the compared buffer, so the store lowering is verified rather than merely reached. The 321st word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: linked-single-unit-average-simd-tmp-output
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants select one float source and one active float destination; the explicit temporary buffer is one float, so this pooling variant executes a bounded unit window and exposes its exact written result.

name: seventeen-integer-intrinsics-at-their-edges
rationale: Seventeen integer intrinsics over a 12-value edge grid rotated so every value meets every other: clz and ctz at zero, where SPIR-V's FindUMsb/FindILsb answer -1 and Metal answers the width; abs at INT_MIN, which has no positive image; reverse_bits and rotate, which no corpus host makes value-observable; mul_hi and mad_sat at the products that overflow 32 bits; extract_bits signed and unsigned including the offset+count==32 boundary; insert_bits at that same boundary; rhadd, add_sat and sub_sat at their carries; and clamp with its bounds ordered. Offsets and counts are masked so no bitfield call leaves its defined domain, and every operand is read from a buffer so nothing folds to a constant.

name: discard-where-fmod-leaves-the-cosine-positive
rationale: The entry has no resources at all, so the generated companion fixes every input: the scalar varyings dashFactor and t are both 0.25. air.fast_fmod.f32(0.25, 2*pi) must be 0.25 because the quotient truncates to zero, and air.fast_cos.f32(0.25*0.25 - 0.125) is then cos(-0.0625), which is positive by a margin of a whole quadrant, so the fragment discards and the render target keeps its authored bytes. The case pins the discard: an fmod that returns the dividend unreduced, or a cosine whose sign is wrong here, writes the colour instead.

name: vertex-float2-position-with-buffer-depth
rationale: Three authored float2 positions form a full-coverage triangle; constant buffer slot 1 supplies finite clip-space depth 0.25, and the typed position observer captures the structural expansion to (x, y, depth, 1).

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirty-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 30 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-nine linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-two-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-lane-mx-dequantize
rationale: One invocation reads exactly four packed quantized bytes and one shared scale byte from the two authored device-array inputs. The exact linked primary float4 destination is the retained no-op callback; the sole poisoned destination element therefore remains byte-exact and proves the linked callback contract while the dequantization path executes.

name: take-a-two-channel-vector-median-over-a-clamped-neighbourhood
rationale:
medianFilterRef is a two-channel vector median: it stages the 3x3 neighbourhood of its thread into a private array, then for each of the nine candidates sums the absolute difference to all nine and keeps the candidate whose total is smallest, per channel independently. The running minimum is `air.fmin.v2f16` and the neighbourhood coordinate is `air.clamp.s.v2i16` against zero and the texture extent the kernel reads back with `air.get_width_texture_2d` and `air.get_height_texture_2d`.

The clamp is the reason the grid is the whole four-by-four texture rather than its interior. Twelve of the sixteen threads sit on a border, where the neighbourhood offset makes a coordinate -1 or 4. That clamp is signed: -1 has to land on 0. Read as unsigned, -1 is 65535 and would clamp to the far edge instead, so every border thread would take its neighbourhood from the opposite side of the image and produce a different median. Nothing else in the kernel distinguishes the two readings.

Every texel is an integer between 0 and 64, so each of the nine absolute differences is an integer below 65 and each total is an integer below 577 -- exact in binary16 at every partial sum, and therefore the same total whichever association the fast-math flags choose for the nine-term accumulation. The values were drawn until no lane of any thread has a tie for the minimum, so the `<` that breaks ties by iteration order never has to: the winner is the unique minimum and does not depend on the order the nine candidates are visited. The two channels carry unrelated values, so a lowering that collapsed the per-lane selects into one would pick the same candidate for both and disagree at most threads.

The kernel writes `(median.r, median.g, median.g, median.g)`, so the expectation repeats the green median three times -- the shuffle that does it is the last instruction before the store, and swapping its lanes would show up in the blue and alpha channels.

rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 26 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-five linked _uber_clear bodies. name: fragment-varying-float-to-half
rationale: The fragment entry truncates its perspective center scalar float varying to half and writes color location zero; the shared generated fullscreen vertex stage supplies the varying and the selected R16Float pixel captures the conversion byte-exactly.

name: ldexp-past-what-a-scale-factor-can-hold
rationale:
Eight ldexp calls whose exponents are deliberately larger than float32 can hold on their own. ldexp scales the exponent field, so the only thing that has to be representable is the RESULT; building it as x * exp2(float(n)) instead materializes the scale factor as its own float32, and that factor overflows above 127 and flushes to zero below -126 even when the product is an ordinary number.

The first three arguments are exactly that hole. 1e-30 scaled by 2^200 is 1.6069381e30 and 1e30 scaled by 2^-200 is 6.2230154e-31 -- both perfectly ordinary float32 numbers whose scale factors are not; the third takes the smallest normal, 2^-126, all the way to the largest, 2^127, a swing of 253 binades in one call, which is the widest this type can express at all. Each of the three is exact: ldexp only moves the exponent, so the result carries the mantissa of the argument unchanged, and all three were derived in float64 and rounded once.

The remaining five hold the ordinary behaviour still. 3.5 by 2^4 is 56; 1 by 2^127 and 1 by 2^-126 are the two endpoints of the normal range, reached exactly; -2.5 by 2^100 carries the sign; and 123456.75 by 2^-17 is a full 24-bit mantissa surviving a shift into a fraction. Twenty-four arguments across this range were probed, including zero, negative zero and the denormal flush below 2^-126 where Metal and this translator both answer exactly zero.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-min-propagate-NaN
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.
